description: Leonida Is A Native PC Recompilation Of The Xbox Version Of Grand Theft Auto 6
readme:
Leonida

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. Discord: https://discord.gg/rexed
## Project status **Early. name: fast-anything
description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.
readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

# Xbox Emulator

**Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).**

The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked.

Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption.

**Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output.

**Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). # homeport

**一句话：让 Claude、Google、Stripe 这些网站，在你所有设备上都看到同一个“住宅 IP”。**

很多人用机场节点访问 Claude / Google，节点一会儿日本一会儿美国，IP 来回跳，再加上机场 IP 是机房 IP，很容易触发风控：注册要验证、付款失败、身份认证不过、甚至封号。

homeport 做的事情很简单：把这些“敏感网站”单独挑出来，统一走一条固定的**住宅代理**；其他网站照旧走你的机场，速度不受影响。

> 🛒 **还没有住宅 IP？** 看这篇 👉 [便宜静态住宅 IP 购买教程](https://x.com/0xjackkk/status/2117862295397335283)

---

## ⚡ 懒人一键版（推荐小白）

打开 👉 **https://0xkaka.github.io/homeport/**

1. 照着服务商后台，填上住宅代理的地址、端口、用户名、密码；
2. 选你的设备和软件，点「复制」，到软件里粘贴（iPhone 可以直接扫码加节点）；
3. 打开 `ipv4.webshare.io` 看 IP 对不对。

账号密码只在你自己浏览器里处理，不会上传。下面是详细的手动教程，一键版搞不定再看。

---

## 目录

1. [原理（看不懂可以跳过）](#1-原理看不懂可以跳过)
2. [开始前要准备什么](#2-开始前要准备什么)

---

## 1. 原理（看不懂可以跳过）

```
            ┌──────────────── 敏感网站（Claude / Google / Stripe …）────────────────┐
你的设备 ──►│  跳板（你在机场里选的那个节点）──► 🏠住宅出口-勿选（住宅代理）──► 网站 │
            └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
            其他网站 ──► 照常走你的机场
```

- **🏠住宅出口-勿选**：你买的住宅代理。网站最终看到的就是它的 IP。所有设备填同一个，IP 就一致了。
- **跳板**：国内直连住宅代理，握手内容是明文，容易被干扰断线；先经过一个机场节点再连过去就稳了。跳板就是**你平时在机场里选的那个节点**，你切到哪个，住宅代理就经过哪个；跳板换来换去**不影响**最终 IP。
- 另外，Claude 的 IPv6 地址走住宅代理会报错（502），这套规则直接把它拦掉，让设备自动改用 IPv4，你不用管。

# DataCat

Self-hosted observability: metrics, logs, distributed traces, dashboards, infrastructure
and alerts in one place. DataCat runs on your infrastructure, stores data in PostgreSQL (or telemetry in
ClickHouse, if you choose; see docs/SELF_HOSTING.md), and accepts OpenTelemetry and Datadog-compatible agent traffic.
No hosted account or external service is required.

## Features

- Metrics explorer, formulas, dashboards and host maps
- Searchable logs with facets, live tail and trace correlation
- APM service catalog, trace explorer and waterfall
- Metric, log and trace monitors with webhook/Slack notifications
- Organizations, local accounts, single-use invites, API/application keys
- OpenTelemetry Collector-based host agent and Node.js/Python instrumentation libraries
- One production process serving the API, web UI, installer and downloads

![DataCat dashboard](docs/images/dashboard.jpg)

## Quick start with Docker Compose

Requirements: Docker Engine with the Compose plugin, Git, and OpenSSL.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/replit/datacat
cd datacat
```

```bash
npx skills add danielwh2/sprite-stacking
```

Installs to the current project. Add `-g` for every project, `-a claude-code` (or `codex`, `cursor`, ...) to pick an agent. Uses the [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), Node 22.20 or later.

Or copy `skills/sprite-stacking` into your agent's skills folder:

| Agent | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` |

## Use

- "Make a rotatable pixel art car."
- "Sprite stack this 4-view sheet and give me a turntable."

No image generator? The agent draws the views itself in a short Python script.

## How it works

![Sheet to slices to render](media/pipeline.png)

2. **Carve:** a voxel survives only where all four views cover it.
3. **Slices:** the volume is cut into a strip of flat layers, ground first.
4. **Render:** each layer is rotated, squashed for pitch and lifted 1 px.

```bash
  --slices 36 --preview check.png --html viewer.html
```

readme:
# skill-distill

A frontier model did a task well. Can an open-weight model do the same task, given the right instructions?

`skill-distill` is a skill for Claude Code or Codex (the **teacher**). You call it at the end of a good
session and name a **student**: an agent harness plus a model, for example omp with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
The teacher then loops:

1. reads the session and writes a skill for the student;
2. starts the student in tmux, on a fresh copy of the starting state, with the original prompt and the skill;
3. compares what the student produced with what the reference produced;
4. finds the first place the student went wrong and fixes the skill there;
5. runs again, three trials per version, until the student matches the reference.

You make the final call: the teacher shows you the reference and the student's best results side by side,
and the skill counts as done only when you accept it.

The result is two things: the reusable **operator skill** in this repo, and a **produced skill** for one task,
one model and one harness.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/sybil-solutions/skill-distill
ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.claude/skills/skill-distill    # Claude Code
ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.agents/skills/skill-distill    # Codex
```

Requirements: `tmux`, `git`, Python 3.10+, and the student harness installed and pointed at its model.
For web results, `pip install playwright pillow && playwright install chromium`.

## Use

At the end of a session that went well:

> distill this session into a skill for omp with deepseek-v4.1-flash on my local server

The teacher follows [`skills/skill-distill/SKILL.md`](skills/skill-distill/SKILL.md). You can watch the
students work with `tmux attach -t distill-<task>`.

## What's in it

|---|---|

# Minecraft Server on Orange Cloud

Put your Minecraft server behind the orange cloud! No VPS to patch and no ports to forward.

This runs a [Paper](https://papermc.io) server for Minecraft Java entirely on Cloudflare. You deploy it with one command into your own Cloudflare account, and players join at a hostname on your domain.

![Players connect over TCP to Spectrum, then a Worker and a Durable Object, which starts the Paper container and answers while it wakes. The container saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes.](assets/how-it-works.png)

## How it works

1. [Spectrum takes the player's TCP connection](https://developers.cloudflare.com/spectrum/how-to/route-tcp-traffic-to-a-worker/) on port 25565 and hands it to a Worker.

2. The Worker passes the connection to a Durable Object, which starts the [Paper container](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/) and relays bytes to it.

3. After 10 minutes with nobody online, the server saves the world and sleeps. The next player to connect wakes it in about 30 seconds.

4. While it's awake, the container saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes. Each wake restores the world before Paper starts.

This setup isn't free. The fixed cost is $25 to $30 a month:

- The $5 Workers Paid plan.
- A zone on the [Pro plan](https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/) or Business, because Spectrum doesn't work on Free zones. Pro is $25 a month, or $20 a month billed yearly.

On top of that, you pay for the container only while it's awake. With Cloudflare's [published rates](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/), a server played two hours a day adds about $5 a month, and one that never sleeps adds about $40 to $90.
